attribution_limitations: The abstract and Table 1 give different baseline probing depths for the mesial-buccal site of the examined canine.

The abstract names the examined tooth the left maxillary canine while the case text and Table 1 use tooth 23; the case text calls tooth 23 the canine, so the abstract gingival recession is merged into the tooth 23 condition. The FDI number-to-name mapping itself is not printed.

The abstract calls the first treatment step full-mouth debridement and the case text calls the first phase generalized scaling and root planing; both name the first step of the same treatment together with oral hygiene instructions, so they are one procedure fact.
The discussion gives a 6-month root coverage of 91% while the case text and abstract give 91.7%; this reads as rounding.

The text reports no increase in probing depth (3mm) and 2.5 of GR at the 2-year and 18-year intervals without naming a site and without a unit for 2.5; only the Figure 5A caption prints 2.5 mm for 2 years. Table 1 gives per-site 2-year values but the text does not cite it.

The author hypothesizes that orthodontic treatment caused the gingival recession and proposes that orthodontic movement could cause the pulp necrosis; the pulp necrosis is presupposed, the causes are hypotheses.
The sentence about the absence of tooth decay or fillings does not name the tooth, and the same paragraph reports no changes in masticatory habits.

The 6-month text recession (1 mm, root surface) and the 2-year text/caption recession (2.5) name no site and do not cite Table 1; Table 1 prints matching numbers at more than one site (6 months: mid-buccal 1 and distal 1). Matching numbers alone do not make them the same measurement.
